_comment: Spoken deliveries of seed-bank points, for calibrating the coverage thresholds against the real embedder. `deliveries` are how someone actually says that point out loud — never verbatim, because nobody reads their own bullets aloud. `only` names the points that may be struck: a false strike-through is worse than a missed one, since the user skips something they never said. `nearMisses` are on-topic speech that says none of the points. `windows` are points delivered across two breaths, which no single segment covers.

deliveries.text: The riskiest part was two complainants against one long-tenured supervisor, at a site that was used to keeping people quiet.
First thing I did was separate the people rather than the payroll — schedule changes, nobody suspended.
I ran eleven interviews over five days and I documented each one as I went.
The decision held up in the end — there was no grievance and no appeal.
I start by showing them their own attrition and overtime figures, because those tell the story better than I can.
Then I coach the behaviour rather than the intention — almost none of them mean to burn anyone out.
And I set a review date, because coaching without a checkpoint is really just a hope.
On day one I name what it actually costs people, honestly — they can smell spin.
I give the managers the reason in their own numbers, not in HR's language.
And we publish the exception path, because that pressure needs somewhere to go.
In the first twenty-four hours I scope it and put interim measures in place.
The order matters: complainant first, then the witnesses, and the respondent last.
Then I close the loop with both sides, because silence reads like a cover-up.
I triage on legal exposure first and people risk second.
Every file gets one owner — I don't run anything out of a shared inbox.
The first rollout missed the night shift completely.
The optics of the security escort cost us that site's trust for a whole quarter.
We keep one national floor with provincial overlays on top — never ten separate policies.
Usually I can offer the compliant version of the same outcome they wanted.
The onboarding rebuild is exactly the kind of work I want more of.

nearMisses.text: In the end the supervisor left the business a few months later.

It was a return-to-office policy and nobody wanted it.

Leadership does not usually put it that bluntly.
